source_text: Κἀγὼ εἶπον· Ὡς ὑμῖν φίλον, πράξω. Ἀπὸ μὲν οὖν τῶν ἐξηγήσεων, ὧν ἐξηγήσατο Ἔσδρας εἰς τὸν νόμον τὸν περὶ τοῦ πάσχα, τὴν ἐξήγησιν ταύτην ἀφείλοντο· Καὶ εἶπεν Ἔσδρας τῷ λαῷ· Τοῦτο τὸ πάσχα ὁ σωτὴρ ἡμῶν καὶ ἡ καταφυγὴ ἡμῶν. Καὶ ἐὰν διανοηθῆτε καὶ ἀναβῇ ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν, ὅτι μέλλομεν αὐτὸν ταπεινοῦν ἐν σημείῳ, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐλπίσωμεν ἐπ᾿ αὐτόν, οὐ μὴ ἐρημωθῇ ὁ τόπος οὗτος εἰς τὸν ἅπαντα χρόνον, λέγει ὁ θεὸς τῶν δυνάμεων· ἂν δὲ μὴ πιστεύσητε αὐτῷ μηδὲ εἰσακούσητε τοῦ κηρύγματος αὐτοῦ. ἔσεσθε ἐπίχαρμα τοῖς ἔθνεσι [Esdr. ?]. Καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν διὰ Ἱερεμίου λεχθέντων ταῦτα περιέκοψαν· Ἐγὼ ὡς ἀρνίον ἄκακον. φερόμενον τοῦ θύεσθαι. Ἐπ᾿ ἐμὲ ἐλογίζοντο λογισμόν, λέγοντες· Δεῦτε, ἐμβάλωμεν ξύλον εἰς τὸν ἄρτον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκτρίψωμεν αὐτὸν ἐκ γῆς ζώντων, καὶ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ οὐ μὴ μνησθῇ οὐκέτι [JÉR., XI, 19]. Καὶ ἐπειδὴ αὕτη ή περικοπή, ἡ ἐκ τῶν λόγων τοῦ Ἱερεμίου, ἔτι ἐστὶν ἐγγεγραμμένη ἔν τισιν ἀντιγράφοις τῶν ἐν συναγωγαῖς Ἰουδαίων (πρὸ γὰρ ὀλίγου χρόνου ταῦτα ἐξέκοψαν), ἐπειδὰν καὶ ἐκ τούτων τῶν λόγων ἀποδεικνύηται ὅτι ἐβουλεύσαντο Ἰουδαῖοι περὶ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἀναιρεῖν αὐτὸν σταυρώσαντες βουλευσάμενοι, καὶ αὐτὸς μηνύεται, ὡς καὶ διὰ τοῦ Ἡσαΐου προεφητεύθη, ὡς πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἀγόμενος , καὶ ἐνθάδε ὡς ἀρνίον ἄκακον δηλοῦται· ὥστ᾿ ἀπορούμενοι ἐπὶ τὸ βλασφημεῖν χωροῦσι. Καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν λόγων τοῦ αὐτοῦ Ἱερεμίου ὁμοίως ταῦτα περιέκοψαν· Ἐμνήσθη δὲ κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἅγιος Ἰσραὴλ τῶν νεκρῶν αὐτοῦ, τῶν κεκοιμημένων εἰς γῆν χώματος, καὶ κατέβη πρὸς αὐτοὺς εὐαγγελίσασθαι αὐτοῖς τὸ σωτήριον αὐτοῦ [JÉR. ? cf. I Pierre, III, 19, et IV. 6].
pass_a_gloss: And I said, As it is pleasing to you, I will do. Therefore, from the explanations that Ezra explained concerning the law of the passover, they removed this explanation: And Ezra said to the people, This passover is our Savior and our refuge. And if you think and it comes into your heart that we are about to humble Him in a sign, and after these things we hope in Him, this place will not be deserted for all time, says the God of powers; but if you do not believe in Him nor listen to His proclamation, you will be a mockery to the nations. And from the things spoken through Jeremiah, they cut out these words: I am like an innocent lamb being led to be slaughtered. They devised a plan against me, saying, Come, let us put wood into his bread and destroy him from the land of the living, and his name will not be remembered anymore. And since this passage, from the words of Jeremiah, is still written in some copies of the Jewish synagogues (for they cut these out a short time ago), when it is also demonstrated from these words that the Jews planned to kill Christ by crucifying Him, having taken counsel, and He Himself is indicated, as also prophesied through Isaiah, as a sheep being led to slaughter, and here as an innocent lamb He is revealed; thus, being at a loss, they proceed to blaspheme. And from the words of the same Jeremiah, they similarly cut out these words: And the Lord, the holy God, remembered Israel, His dead, who slept in the earth of dust, and He went down to them to proclaim the gospel of His salvation to them.

pass_b_english: I replied that I would do as they wished. Consequently, the editors removed from the expositions with which Ezra expounded the law concerning the Passover this particular interpretation: Ezra told the people, 'This Passover is our Savior and our refuge (Esdras). If you reflect and take to heart that we are about to humble Him in a sign, and after these things place your hope in Him, this place shall not be deserted for all time, declares the God of hosts; but if you do not believe in Him nor listen to His proclamation, you will become a mockery to the nations.'

They likewise cut out the following words from the prophecies spoken through Jeremiah: 'I was like an innocent lamb led to the slaughter. They devised a plan against me, saying, "Come, let us put wood into his bread and destroy him from the land of the living, and let his name be remembered no more"' (Jeremiah 11:19). Since this passage from Jeremiah is still found in some copies of the Jewish synagogue scrolls — for they excised it only a short time ago — it also demonstrates from these very words that the Jews plotted to kill the Christ by crucifying Him, having taken counsel together, and that He Himself is revealed as the one prophesied through Isaiah as a sheep led to slaughter, and here as an innocent lamb; thus, finding themselves at a loss, they resort to blasphemy.

And from the words of the same Jeremiah they similarly removed these words: 'The Lord, the holy God of Israel, remembered His dead, those who slept in the earth of dust, and He went down to them to proclaim the gospel of His salvation to them' (Jeremiah, cf. 1 Peter 3:19 and 4:6).

review.notes: Pass B fails on a negation/meaning error in the Jeremiah quote. The Greek says 'οὐ μὴ μνησθῇ οὐκέτι' (his name will not be remembered anymore), which Pass A correctly translates. However, Pass B translates this as 'let his name be remembered no more', which is a positive imperative/wish rather than the negative indicative/future of the Greek text. Additionally, Pass B omits 'Ἰσραὴλ' (Israel) in the final Jeremiah quote ('ὁ θεὸς ἅγιος Ἰσραὴλ'), whereas Pass A correctly includes it ('the holy God, remembered Israel').
reasons: Pass B misrepresents the negation in the Jeremiah quote: 'οὐ μὴ μνησθῇ οὐκέτι' (his name will not be remembered anymore) is rendered as 'let his name be remembered no more', changing the mood and sense.
Pass B omits 'Ἰσραὴλ' in the final clause: 'ὁ θεὸς ἅγιος Ἰσραὴλ' (the holy God, remembered Israel) is rendered as 'The Lord, the holy God of Israel', which shifts the grammatical object/apposition.

review.notes: greek/justin_dialogue.xml: "Καὶ εἶπεν Ἔσδρας τῷ λαῷ· Τοῦτο τὸ πάσχα ὁ σωτὴρ ἡμῶν καὶ ἡ καταφυγὴ ἡμῶν."; Pass A: "And Ezra said to the people, 'This Passover is our Savior and our refuge (Esdras).'"; Pass B: "Ezra told the people, 'This Passover is our Savior and our refuge (Esdras).'"
reasons: Pass A and Pass B both incorrectly attribute the quote 'This passover is our Savior and our refuge' to Ezra, but the Greek text says 'And Ezra said to the people...' which is not the same as 'Ezra told the people...' or 'Ezra said to the people...' as in the translations. The Greek text is more direct and does not use the phrasing 'told the people' or 'said to the people' as in the translations. Additionally, the scripture citation for Esdras is not present in the Greek text, and the citation is incorrectly placed in the middle of the quote in both translations.
